narrative.overview:
DitoOS treats the portfolio as a personal Windows 95/98 inspired workspace. Teal wallpaper, colored pixel icons, gray beveled software controls and navy-to-blue title bars establish the period identity. Bitmap labels make the interface feel familiar; Verdana gives project narratives a clear, readable voice that fits the era. A darker teal entry ground frames the supplied portrait as a reversible dot field, adding a personal signature within the same software world.

Depth expresses software state: a raised button can be pressed, a title bar identifies the active window, and a sunken field accepts input. Motion guides entry and reveals desktop icons, with a skip path so visitors stay in control.
keyCharacteristics: Teal desktop surrounding warm off-white content.
Square beveled controls and active blue title bars.
Original colored pixel artwork on a 48 × 48 grid.
Bitmap interface labels paired with readable Verdana stories.
Reversible static-photo dot reveal with keyboard and touch alternatives.

rules.name: The Active Window Rule
rules.body: Use the navy-to-blue gradient for the active title bar; inactive windows use the observed gray gradient.

rules.name: The Reading Rule
rules.body: Use the bitmap face for interface labels and Verdana for narrative content; article copy stays at a maximum of 65ch.

rules.name: The Software Depth Rule
rules.body: Bevels communicate raised or sunken controls; do not replace them with rounded ambient cards.

rules.name: The Reversible Portrait Rule
rules.body: Use the supplied static portrait; preserve tap and keyboard full reveal and the reduced-motion original-photo fallback. No webcam stream or camera permission is implemented.

dos: Do keep controls and window chrome square and beveled.
Do use bitmap UI text for labels and Verdana for extended reading.
Do preserve readable content and usable controls at mobile widths.
Do use the original crisp-edged pixel icon family consistently.
Do keep visible focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Do preserve touch and keyboard alternatives for the portrait.
Do keep Canvas work event-driven and pause it when out of view.
donts: Don't replace the approved desktop world with a modern marketing template.
Don't apply pixel typography to long project narratives.
Don't use blur or smooth interpolation on pixel artwork.
Don't make motion necessary to access content.
Don't represent the static portrait effect as a live webcam.
Don't hide Guest entry or the direct path to projects behind the name field.
